subject: Private observability: SIEM proxy resilience & trace correlation checklist

Subject: Observability export questions for private deployment

Jordan,

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier. A couple of items popped up from our security and SOC teams as we scope evidence delivery for our private (VPC) deployment:

- We need an architecture that minimizes attack surface when forwarding logs to our Splunk HECs inside the customer VPC. Can you outline proxy patterns you support (TLS termination, MTLS, forwarder vs HEC consumer)?
- How do you recommend preserving trace correlation between application traces and Redwood-generated request traces (headers to preserve, sampling considerations)?
- Our auditors require proof of robust backpressure handling and no silent data loss during peak inflight batches. Can you provide examples/runbooks for failover and replay?

We have a proof-of-concept Splunk HEC cluster in staging; I can share collector endpoints. Prefer a short checklist we can include in the compliance packet.

Appreciate it — Emily
Emily Rogers
Head of SOC Operations, Globex Financial
E: erogers@globex.com
T: +1 (415) 555-0192

Emily — thanks, good set of questions. I pulled Kim and Marissa in; below is a concise checklist we can commit to for your compliance packet. We'll follow up with a short call to validate the HEC endpoints and run a chứng file transfer test.

Quick checklist (draft):
1) Connection model: support for outbound MTLS from Redwood forwarder to customer HEC, or inbound HEC pull behind customer proxy. Prefer MTLS when mutual auth is required.
2) Encryption & auth: TLS1.3 with client cert rotation documented; optional use of customer HSM for private keys on on-prem appliances.
3) Delivery guarantees: at-least-once delivery with persistent local queueing and configurable retry/backoff. Replay utilities for forensic re-delivery.
4) Backpressure: TCP backpressure + HEC 429 handling; circuit-breaker and local buffering to avoid silent drops.
5) Tracing correlation: preserve X-Trace-ID / traceparent headers and map Redwood request_id -> trace_id in metadata. Provide sample tracehook mapping.
6) Audit evidence: per-batch ACK logs, delivery receipts, and a daily digest for SOC.
7) Hardening: firewall rules (egress to specific HEC IPs/ports), short-lived creds, and IP allowlist for the forwarder.

Kim — can you add two practical snippets (HEC curl example and a tracehook header mapping) and confirm default batch size / disk queue sizing we recommend for Globex staging? Marissa — can you own the evidence artifact (digest + sample logs) we will attach to the packet?

Proposed next steps:
- Short call Wed 10:00 PT to validate HEC endpoints and run a small end-to-end test
- Deliver checklist + sample artifacts by COB Fri

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Splunk Professional Services <ps@splunk.com>

Hi Jordan / Emily,

Quick clarifications from the Splunk PS side:
- If using HEC we recommend persistent TCP with MTLS where possible; HEC will return 200/ HTTP 429 for throttling which should be surfaced to the forwarder.
- For trace linkage, Splunk APM accepts distributed trace headers (traceparent, tracestate) and we can map a custom header (X-Redwood-RequestId) to a field in Splunk during ingest.
- For large batch writes, set max_content_length to avoid rejection; recommend max 1MB per event payload and 10k events per batch as default ceiling.

We can join Wed and bring an HEC staging collector for the end-to-end test. Sharing a quick doc: https://docs.splunk.com/HEC/private-deploy-best-practices

Cheers,
Lina Park
Eng Manager, Splunk Professional Services

On Mon, Jul 8, 2029 at 11:03 AM Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Emily — thanks, good set of questions. I pulled Kim and Marissa in; below is a concise checklist we can commit to for your compliance packet.

Adding the technical specifics requested below. I attached a tiny text file with tracehook header snippets (tracehook-snippets.txt).

- Recommended default batch sizing: 5k events / 500KB payload; adjustable per deployment. Disk queue sizing: allow for 10 minutes of peak traffic at your p95 QPS (we typically recommend N*p95*avg_event_size).
- Retry/backoff: exponential backoff with jitter; retry window configurable (default 24h) and persisted on local disk for on-prem forwarder.
- MTLS details: client cert CN must be Rotating: redwood-forwarder-<customer>-<env>-YYYYMMDD; server cert validation with CRL/OCSP optional.
- Backpressure handling: we surface HEC 429 as transient; we stop consuming upstream only when local storage exceeds threshold and emit an alert.
- Tracehook mapping: preserve traceparent and also inject X-Redwood-RequestId mapped to field redwood_request_id in the HEC metadata. Example header snippet in attachment.

Example HEC curl (quick):
curl -k -H "Authorization: Splunk <HEC_TOKEN>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -H "traceparent: 00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-00" 
  -d '{"event":"test","redwood_request_id":"rwd-12345","severity":"info"}' \
  https://staging-hec.globex.internal:8088/services/collector/event/1.0

I'll confirm the exact default disk queue numbers after I look at Globex staging p95 numbers.

—Kim
Kimberly Park
Principal Infrastructure Security Engineer | Redwood Inference
